chunks: Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the flesh of predatory animals among birds and beasts. He said:
"As for eating their meat, we dislike it; but as for the skins, ride upon them, and do not wear anything from them in which you pray."

key_terms.الطَّيْرِ: birds, here referring to predatory birds
key_terms.فَارْكَبُوا: use them for riding or mounted use
key_terms.لُحُومِ: the meats or flesh being asked about
key_terms.نَكْرَهُهُ: we dislike it, indicating karāhah in this context

ai.seo_question: Can the skins of predatory animals be used or worn during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about predatory animals among birds and beasts. It states dislike for eating their meat, while permitting use of their skins for riding or similar benefit, but forbidding wearing such skins in salat (prayer).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.805 - Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) regarding eating the meat of wild animals, including birds and other beasts.
Imam responded, "As for eating their meat, we dislike it, but as for their skins, you may use them to ride on but do not wear anything made from them for prayer."
